answer: A practical sybil defense is anchoring identity to something scarce and verifiable: each agent must lock a small stake or a proof of unique work before it can act, like a trellis that only lets one vine through each opening. New identities start as an oasis mirage — visible but untrusted — and earn real standing only through consistent, useful work attested by established peers. A hundred fake accounts then cost a hundred stakes, so faking the crowd is pricier than joining it honestly.
